entries.text: A single heart wakes the glade
Tap a conduit to turn it. Light every sleeping critter.
Two hearts, two hues, no mixing
Critters only wake to their own colour. Keep the streams apart.
Blend the light, wake the deep grove
Joined hearts blend: red plus green makes gold. Keep the blue stream to itself.
Three streams, and conduits that will not last
Some conduits crumble after a few turns. Plan the route before you spin.
Two streams, and roots that run beneath both
Conduits wearing the same pips share a root. Turn one and its partners turn with it.
Wake the grove without waking the dark
Duskcaps sleep in the shade. Light one and the glade will not settle, so route around them.
One ring of light around a sleeping dark
The ring's four corners share one root. Its edges are what can leak light inward.
Two streams, and a thicket between them
The thicket is the wall keeping the streams apart. Open it and you lose both at once.
Gold, teal, and a red spring of its own
Gold and teal both carry green. Join those two and both go white together.
Everything the grove taught you, at once
One root reaches into all four corners. Nothing here can be solved a corner at a time.

Only the {0} glades below count, and only the first time you finish one inside the window — a glade you cleared before the event opened is one you have already been paid for. There are {1} blooms along the vine, worth {2} credits between them.

A bloom opens the moment you reach it, and then it waits. Come back and tap it and the credits are yours. Tapping a bloom higher up the vine takes every open one below it at the same time, so nothing can be left behind.

Two flows pass through this tile and never meet. It wears no hub, and that is how you tell it from a junction: follow each strand with your eye, because light that enters by one arm can only leave by the arm that shares its strand.
One tile, and two streams that never meet
A crossing carries two flows past each other. Turn it the other way and both hearts pour into one channel.
A rope of light, twisted three times
The two runs change lanes at every crossing. One left the wrong way round hands a heart's light to the other's critters.
The shadow runs straight through the grove
A duskcap's path used to have to go around the light. Across a crossing it can go under it instead.
The upper crossing crumbles after two turns and needs one. You are allowed exactly one wrong guess about which way it goes.
Two crossings, one root, opposite corners
Bound conduits turn as one, crossings included. The tap that settles the near braid settles the far one with it.
Three networks share this ground. Two stay pure and the third holds a heart of each, and the crossings are what let all three pass.
The dark fords the light three times
Every crossing here is a place the shadow and the grove could be joined by mistake. Read which arm belongs to which strand before you turn.
These crossings are rooted where they stand. The grove is not asking which way they face — it is asking what still fits through them.
A cascade, handed on at every span
Yellow gives the grove to red, red to green and green to blue, and every hand-over happens inside one tile.
Everything the vale has taught, tied once
Three networks, a shadow through all of them, two crossings on one root and brittle stone on the only ways in.
